findings.evidence: `rg "nullspace|Nullspace" mathlib/Mathlib` finds no Mathlib declaration names, only prose; `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean:979-980` has `apply_apply_same_eq_zero_iff ... : B x x = 0 ↔ x ∈ LinearMap.ker B`, and this PR’s line 80 is exactly `LinearMap.ker (positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm K)`.
findings.fix: Rename the submodule and dependent lemmas to use standard `ker` terminology, e.g. `positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer`, `mem_positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer`, and replace `_mem_nullspace` suffixes by `_mem_...Ker`/`_mem_ker` consistently.
findings.issue: `positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppNullspace` and all derived theorem names use `nullspace`, but the declaration is definitionally `LinearMap.ker (positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm K)` and Mathlib’s sesquilinear-form API states the same zero-diagonal characterization with `x ∈ LinearMap.ker B`, not a nullspace name.

summary: The new API uses nonstandard `nullspace` terminology for an object Mathlib names as a kernel/radical of a sesquilinear form.
